PP.SRI.SANAL.P.RAJ  THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 26.03.2026, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 Crl.M.C No.2553 of 2026  2026:KER:26973  -2- Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 26 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43382860/
1  ORDER (Dated this the 26th day of March, 2026)

The petitioner who is the accused in S.C No.926 of 2024 pending before the Fast Track Special Court, Kodungallur, arising out of Crime No.906 of 2023 of Kodungallur Police Station, filed this Crl.M.C under Section 528 BNSS praying for setting aside Annexure-A6 order passed by the learned Sessions Judge by which an application filed under Section 311 Cr.PC for recalling PWs1 and 2 was dismissed.

2. The petitioner is facing trial for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 450, 354,
354(A)(1)(i) and 376(2)
(n) of IPC and Sections 4 r/w Section 3(a), 6(1) r/w Section 5(I), 12 r/w Section 11(iv)(v) of POCSO Act and Sections 64(A) and 67(a)
(b) of IT Act.
3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, now the prosecution evidence is almost over and the Investigating Officer alone remains to be examined.

The petitioner filed Annexure-A4 application before the trial Court for recalling PWs1 and 2 on the ground that:
"Subsequent to their examination, certain material aspects and clarifications, having a bearing on the proper appreciation of the evidence already on record, have come to the notice of the defence."
The details of the alleged material aspects and clarification sought to be put to PWs1 and 2 were not disclosed either in Annexure-A4 or at the time of arguments.
Therefore, it can be seen that the prayer in Annexure-A4 application is only general and vague and as such, from the above application, the relevancy of recalling PWs1 and 2 could not be ascertained.
In the absence of any such specific reason for recalling PWs1 and 2, I do not find any grounds to interfere with Annexure- A6 order and accordingly, this Crl.

Sd/-
C.
